eventMetadata.context_description: The Detroit Pistons forced a decisive Game 7 against the Orlando Magic in their Eastern Conference first-round NBA playoffs series, tied 3-3, after a historic 24-point comeback win 93-79 in Game 6 on May 1 at Kia Center. Momentum swings toward Detroit as the No. 1 seed hosts Game 7 on May 3, with Cade Cunningham's playmaking pivotal amid recent form showing resilience. Orlando's defense, a season strength, faces pressure without Franz Wagner (calf strain, out since Game 4) and Jonathan Isaac (knee, sidelined), thinning their frontcourt. Pistons center Jalen Duren suffered a hand injury in Game 6 but returned; official injury report pending could impact paint battle and rebounding edge. Home-court advantage and rest factor favor Detroit in this elimination matchup.

eventMetadata.context_description: In the Western Conference first-round playoffs, the Lakers hold a precarious 3-2 series lead over the Rockets heading into Game 6 at Houston's Toyota Center, where LA led big after three quarters amid ongoing injury woes. Luka Dončić remains sidelined for the Lakers with a hamstring strain not expected until potential Game 7, while the Rockets battle without Kevin Durant (ankle), Fred VanVleet (ACL tear), and Steven Adams (ankle). Houston's youth movement—Amen Thompson, Tari Eason, Alperen Şengün—sparked back-to-back wins in Games 4 (115-96 rout) and 5 (99-93 grinder) via turnover-forcing defense (exploiting LA's 17.8 per 100 possessions) and rebounding edge. LeBron James (22.2 PPG, 8.0 APG) carries LA, boosted by Austin Reaves' rusty Game 5 return (22 points off bench), but high-stakes closeout pressure looms.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Cleveland Cavaliers and Toronto Raptors head to a decisive Game 7 in their Eastern Conference first-round NBA playoffs series, tied 3-3, with Cleveland hosting at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse on May 3. Raptors' resilience shone in Thursday's Game 6 home win via RJ Barrett's game-winner in overtime, overcoming the absence of Immanuel Quickley (hamstring, out for series) and Brandon Ingram (right heel inflammation, missed Game 6). Scottie Barnes delivered key scoring despite bumps. Cavaliers, bolstered by James Harden's efficiency and Evan Mobley's interior presence, hold home-court advantage after a 125-120 Game 5 triumph; their roster remains healthier overall, with no major injury concerns. Momentum favors Toronto's grit, but Cleveland's depth and Donovan Mitchell's playoff form loom large.

eventMetadata.context_description: France holds a slim trader consensus edge at 16% implied probability to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup, buoyed by explosive attacking depth led by Kylian Mbappé and Didier Deschamps' proven knockout pedigree from 2018 and the 2022 final, despite Hugo Ekitike's season-ending Achilles rupture. Spain trails closely at 15%, reflecting Euro 2024 triumph and Lamine Yamal's anticipated recovery from a hamstring injury that sidelined him for Barcelona's finale, though striker Samu Aghehowa's earlier ACL tear adds concern. The race stays tight among England (11%), Argentina, and Brazil (both 9%) amid widespread injuries—Rodrygo and Éder Militão out for Brazil, aging Lionel Messi for Argentina—compounded by the expanded 48-team format's chaotic group stage paths and cross-continental travel in the June-July heat.

title: Counter-Strike: G2 vs FaZe (BO3) - BLAST Rivals Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the Counter-Strike Quarterfinal 1 match between G2 and FaZe in the BLAST Rivals Playoffs, initially scheduled for May 1 at 3:30PM ET.

This market will resolve to "G2" if G2 win the match against FaZe.

This market will resolve to "FaZe" if FaZe win the match against G2.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins.

eventMetadata.context_description: FaZe advanced to the BLAST Rivals Season 1 semifinals with a 2-1 BO3 quarterfinal upset over G2 yesterday at Fort Worth's Dickies Arena, securing Dust2 13-11 and Mirage 16-13 after dropping Ancient 9-13. G2 carried Swiss stage momentum from dominating Astralis, while FaZe built bracket positioning through group stage wins—their first playoffs since Budapest—with no roster changes, patch shifts, or meta disruptions altering dynamics.

eventMetadata.context_description: Weibo Gaming holds a dominant historical edge over Invictus Gaming, winning 14 of 18 head-to-head BO3 series, including a 2-1 victory in their first LPL 2026 Split 2 Group Ascend matchup on April 15. Preceding their May 1 clash, WBG sat 7th in Group Ascend standings at 3-6 (9-13 game record), buoyed by a recent 2-0 upset over Top Esports, while IG occupied 6th at 3-5 (8-11) after a 0-2 sweep by Anyone's Legend. IG's offseason roster overhaul—adding JiaQi, Breathe, and Fury—has shown flashes but inconsistent results amid a four-match skid. With top-four spots securing playoff berths in the double round-robin format, trader consensus reflects WBG's macro play and momentum advantages in the current patch meta favoring structured teamfights.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: US-Iran negotiations for a permanent peace deal remain stalled after President Trump declared dissatisfaction with Tehran's latest proposal submitted via Pakistani mediators, straining the fragile ceasefire amid heightened rhetoric over sanctions and the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Initial high-level talks in Islamabad in mid-April collapsed without agreement on Iran's nuclear enrichment limits or proxy activities, prompting multiple ceasefire extensions but no breakthrough on core disputes like ballistic missiles and regional influence. Traders reflect low implied probabilities for near-term resolution, citing historical mistrust, Iran's supreme leader's rejection of full concessions, and US demands for verifiable denuclearization. Upcoming diplomatic efforts or escalation risks, including potential military actions, loom before May deadlines.

markets.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $150 in May?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President J.D. Vance and HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. dominate trader consensus for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, with RFK Jr. edging ahead at 49% implied probability amid his recent congressional testimony exposing alleged Big Pharma influence on Democrats, boosting his populist appeal on health policy and vaccines among GOP base voters. Vance's 39% reflects his frontrunner status as Trump's heir apparent, reinforced by Iowa visits this week laying early caucus groundwork despite some polling slips. Secretary of State Marco Rubio's 21% surge ties to his strong 35% CPAC straw poll finish last month and donor backing, signaling a contested open primary shaped by 2026 midterms and Trump allies' endorsements.

title: Fed Decision in June?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's June 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for June 16-17, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their June meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Polymarket traders price a 95.5% implied probability of no change to the federal funds rate at the June 16-17 FOMC meeting, reflecting strong consensus driven by the Federal Reserve's April 29 decision to hold steady at 3.50%-3.75% in an 8-4 vote amid hotter March 2026 CPI (3.3% year-over-year, up from 2.4%) and resilient nonfarm payrolls (+178,000). Chair Powell emphasized persistent inflation pressures and labor market strength in his post-meeting remarks, aligning with CME FedWatch odds near 98% for status quo. This positioning could face challenges from upcoming April CPI data (May 12 release) showing sharper cooling or weakening jobless claims, potentially reviving 25 basis point cut odds currently at 3.9%.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus favors California Governor Gavin Newsom at 26.5% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, driven by his executive experience, national visibility from Trump-era clashes, and leads in polls like Emerson College and a March Politico California primary survey where he trounced Kamala Harris. Harris sits at 10.6% despite an April McLaughlin poll showing her at 29%—a surge tied to her April 10 National Action Network remarks openness to another run—and a Harvard/Harris survey indicating 50% Democratic support, highlighting a discrepancy between polling and skin-in-the-game market pricing that discounts her 2024 loss. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (8.4%) energizes progressives and youth per Yale data, while Jon Ossoff (6.6%) has surged on fundraising buzz. Differentiation hinges on executive records for governors like Newsom, Shapiro, and Whitmer versus congressional profiles; consolidation may follow 2026 midterm results, early fundraising, and Trump administration developments.

title: LoL: Top Esports vs Anyone's Legend (BO3) - LPL Group Ascend
description:
This market refers to the LoL match between Top Esports and Anyone's Legend in the LPL Group Ascend, initially scheduled for May 1 at 5:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Top Esports" if Top Esports win the match against Anyone's Legend.

This market will resolve to "Anyone's Legend" if Anyone's Legend win the match against Top Esports.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

In the upcoming match between Top Esports and Anyone's Legend in the LPL Group Ascend, initially scheduled for May 1 at 5:00AM ET:

This market will resolve to the team that secures the first blood in Game 1.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If Game 1 begins but is not completed, this market will resolve to whichever team secured the first blood prior to stoppage. If the first blood did not occur, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is remade, this market will resolve to whichever team secured the first blood prior to the remake. If the first blood did not occur prior to the remake, resolution will be based on the remade game.

If Game 1 is completed but first blood never occurred, this market will resolve to 50-50.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

title: F1 Drivers' Champion
description:

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes teammates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominate early 2026 driver standings with 72 and 63 points respectively after Antonelli's back-to-back wins in China and Japan, fueling trader consensus on their tight title duel at 31.3% and 30.5% implied probabilities. Mercedes' superior power unit and chassis under new regulations have delivered consistent podiums and race pace advantages, while Russell's recent bad luck with pit stops and technical gremlins has narrowed his gap to just nine points ahead of the Miami Grand Prix. McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri trail with strong but inconsistent results, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc lags on 49 points, and Red Bull's Max Verstappen struggles at 12 points amid energy management woes and poor starts, keeping the championship race intensely competitive.

title: Will the Iranian regime fall by May 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran’s current ruling regime is overthrown, collapsed, or otherwise ceases to govern by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This requires a broad consensus of reporting indicating that core structures of the Islamic Republic (e.g. the office of the Supreme Leader, the Guardian Council, IRGC control under clerical authority) have been dissolved, incapacitated, or replaced by a fundamentally different governing system or otherwise lost de facto power over a majority of the population of Iran. This could occur via revolution, civil war, military coup, or voluntary abdication, but only qualifies if the Islamic Republic no longer exercises sovereign power.

Routine political events such as elections, reforms, or leadership succession do not qualify. Internal coups or power shifts that preserve the Islamic Republic’s core structures also do not qualify. Only a clear break in continuity—such as a new provisional government, revolutionary council, or constitution replacing the Islamic Republic will qualify.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus assigns a 97.4% implied probability to the Iranian regime enduring past May 31, driven by its successful suppression of the 2025–2026 nationwide protests through lethal crackdowns that killed thousands and quelled unrest by mid-January, with no verified resurgence of mass demonstrations or elite defections in the past 30 days. Despite economic pressures from sanctions and the ongoing 2026 Iran war—including U.S. and Israeli airstrikes targeting security forces and infrastructure as recently as late April—the regime maintains street control via loyal Revolutionary Guards, internal cohesion amid reported factional tensions, and a history of surviving uprisings. Realistic shifts could arise from sudden military collapse, widespread security force mutiny, or a diplomatic breakthrough exposing leadership fractures, though none have materialized.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by May 15?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 15, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus heavily favors "No" at 94.5% for Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by May 15, driven by the ongoing US-Iran standoff following February's US-Israeli strikes and Iran's retaliatory blockade. Despite an April 8 ceasefire, commercial transits linger at 5-10% of pre-conflict levels—recently just 7-14 vessels daily versus the normal 120-140—due to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, IRGC enforcement, soaring insurance premiums, and shipper caution. Pentagon testimony on April 21 indicated six months for full clearance, with diplomacy stalled and no de-escalation signals in the past week, underscoring formidable barriers to rapid normalization.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket's 2028 Presidential Election Winner market positions Vice President JD Vance as the slight frontrunner at 21.6% implied probability, ahead of California Governor Gavin Newsom at 17.3% and Secretary of State Marco Rubio at 10.7%, reflecting early positioning in a wide-open field two years before primaries. Vance's edge stems from his incumbency as Trump's VP and strong CPAC straw poll leads in late March 2026, bolstered by a UMass Lowell poll showing him topping Newsom 33%-30%, though recent Iran policy divergences with Rubio have introduced GOP primary competition. Newsom maintains traction via his national book tour and Democratic frontrunner status post-2026 midterm considerations. The tight race persists amid no formal declarations and high uncertainty; 2026 midterms, Trump endorsements, economic indicators, and foreign policy outcomes like Iran tensions could widen gaps or elevate challengers.

title: Brazil Presidential Election
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket slightly favors Senator Flávio Bolsonaro at 43.5% over President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 37.5% to win Brazil's October 4, 2026, presidential election, reflecting late April polls like AtlasIntel/Bloomberg and Datafolha that show the duo statistically tied in first-round and simulated runoff scenarios. This tight race stems from Flávio's rapid consolidation of right-wing support following his father Jair Bolsonaro's ineligibility, avenging the 2022 loss amid persistent voter polarization, while Lula—seeking a fourth nonconsecutive term at age 81—relies on his Workers' Party base despite economic headwinds and a recent police probe into Flávio over alleged defamation. Separation could arise from party conventions naming official candidates, Lula's health updates, economic data releases, or scandals before the likely runoff on October 25.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

title: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding US-Iranian relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count. 

The meeting must be in-person and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices the highest odds for a US-Iran diplomatic meeting by June 30 at 68%, reflecting cautious expectations of resumed in-person negotiations amid a holding ceasefire, while nearer terms lag: May 31 at 50%, May 15 at 33%, and May 5 at 6%. This positioning follows the April collapse of Islamabad talks, where US envoys led by VP JD Vance engaged Iranian officials without agreement on nuclear curbs, sanctions relief, or Strait of Hormuz access. President Trump's April 30 rejection of Tehran's latest proposal—prioritizing Hormuz reopening over uranium enrichment—has stalled momentum, with no next round scheduled despite US naval blockade pressures. Watch mediator updates from Pakistan and Oman for potential breakthroughs.

title: Trump announces US blockade of Hormuz lifted by...?
description:
On April 12, 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will blockade the Strait of Hormuz. You can read more about that here: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-iran-fail-reach-deal-peace-talks-day-negotiations-rcna315918.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if President Trump, the US government, or the US military publicly and officially announces the end of the United States blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Note: this market will resolve solely based on whether a qualifying announcement is made within the specified timeframe. Whether the blockade is effectively enforced or whether maritime traffic resumes absent a qualifying announcement will not be considered.

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by end of April?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and April 30, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for April 30, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.
